description.narrative: The Vientiane Sustainable Urban Transport Project (VSUTP) will improve the quality of life in Vientiane by improving access and mobility. The project will do this by establishing a sustainable urban transport management agency (SUTMA), a high-quality public bus transport system, a parking management system, and a national electronic vehicle registration system, and by improving traffic management and accessibility for pedestrians and nonmotorized transport (NMT). The project promotes gender mainstreaming, greenhouse gas reduction, and public-private partnership.

description.narrative: Improved urban transport operations and capacity in Vientiane

By 2026, 163 public buses operating a 158 km total network in Vientiane Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Procurement of the the 55 e-buses financed under EIB loan has delivered to Vientiane in Q1 2025.
Construction of BRT bus lanes and stations achieved work progress at 98%. Operations, control and maintenance service centers at 95% vs 92% elapsed time.
Following government's notice dated 15 December 2025, removal of the concrete separators to painted line markings that created dedicated bus lanes has been implemented. Consequently, ADB has issued the suspension notice dated 29 December 2025. Data Source: Reports from UTMS
Ridership of public bus services reaches 48,000 per day Achievement: 4000 Progress/Status: Not yet due. Data Source: Reports from bus service providers
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. An urban transport management section (UTMS) for Vientiane established Indicator: 30% of agency staff are female Data Source: Implementation and Monitoring Consultants' reports Actual value:

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: 12.9 km of dedicated BRT bus route infrastructure, including 27 BRT stations operational by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Construction of bus lanes and stations including necessary equipment installations are expected to complete by end of 2025 under CW1A and CW1B (BRT buses lanes).
Construction of BRT bus lane work progress at 98%.
On 15 December 2025, the government issued an instruction notice on the design modifications of the BRT bus lanes and the regular traffic lane. The changes involved replacing the concrete curb separators with painted lines, and the work was to be completed by December 2025. Following government's directive, ADB has issued the suspension notice on 29 December 2025. Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: 24 BRT stations operational Data Source: Vientiane DPWT (Deartment of public works and Tansport) Actual value:

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: 55 buses procured and delivered by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed.
Supply of E-buses financed under EIB loan - E-buses are delivered to Lao PDR in January 2025, they are currently parked at the depot. However, the final inspection is pending until the charging stations, being constructed by CW1C Contractor, the constructions progress at 84.8% and expected to completed by 31 December 2025. Therefore, handover of 55 E-buses is expected by the end of 2025. (The mission stressed the urgent need to install the charging station by 31 July 2025 and to fully charge the buses to prevent potential battery damage. Undertake final inspection for acceptance of all installations by 15 August 2025 -in respond the VCSBE has appointed three senior staff members as coordinators for the members preparing the operation and assigned 10 drivers and five mechanics to take training and practice trial driving of the e-buses as well as to take care of the charging, cleaning, and testing the fleet).
Importance note, at appraisal, the VSUTP anticipated to procure diesel buses, but at implementation stage, the e-buses was the choice. Consequently the number of buses has reduced from 96 buses to 55 buses, and this was approved during the Midterm Review Mission in November 2019. Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: Women comprise 30% BRT operations and maintenance staff by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
The project aims to ensure that 30% of jobs generated from BRT services, operations, and maintenance are allocated to women- the project will set up quota (30%) for women in job advertisement for BRT operation, maintenance and service staff (Target 5, target 6 and target 10 the procurement for BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) operations, station services, and control center management (SPC-1) is ongoing.
Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports

Output: 3. Traffic management in the core area of Vientiane improved Indicator: 7 new traffic signals at key intersections in core area operational and existing signals at 14 intersections upgraded by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Construction of traffic signaling in key intersections in core areas of Vientiane Capital and along BRT bus lens are ongoing. Target to complete by Q2 2026.
Overall physical progress is at 83.7% Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports
Output: 3. Traffic management in the core area of Vientiane improved Indicator: Existing signals at 14 intersections upgraded by 2019 Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports Actual value:

Output: 5. Accessibility for pedestrians and other NMT (non-motorized transport) in the core area of Vientiane improved Indicator: Pedestrian access at 27 BRT stations upgraded by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
In the detail designed of 27 BRT (25 stations) total number safe pedestrian crossings is 161 (37/in CW1A and 124/in CW1B). The current number of safe pedestrian crossing is 82 (40 in CW1A and 42 in CW1B).
Construction of pedestrianization in core areas of Vientiane Capital and around the BRT Stations in progress. Design fully included access for pedestrianization, wheelchair, and disability people. Target to complete by end of 2025. Data Source: UTMS reports

Output: 5. Accessibility for pedestrians and other NMT (non-motorized transport) in the core area of Vientiane improved Indicator: Universal access for wheelchair-bound and visually impaired people provided at 27 BRT stations by 2026 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Construction of pedestrianization in core areas of Vientiane Capital and around the BRT Stations in progress. Design fully included access for pedestrianization, wheelchair, and disability people. Target to complete by end of 2025. Data Source: UTMS reports

Output: 6. Institutional capacity of MPWT and UTMS in establishment and operation of the new urban transport system strengthened Indicator: 10 staff in MPWT report increased knowledge on new technologies to be introduced under the project by 2026 (2017 baseline: 0) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Completed.
Trainings for staffs from MPWT, PWT and UTMS were organized both national and international study tours supported by TRTA resources. Capacity building for staffs will be continue mainly on the job and hands-on by PIC experts.
Data Source: Implementation and monitoring consultants' reports

Output: 6. Institutional capacity of MPWT and UTMS in establishment and operation of the new urban transport system strengthened Indicator: All staff under UTMS report increased knowledge on new technologies and system delivered under the project by 2026 (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Three individual consultants (C4:1 Urban Transport Operation Expert, C4:2 Marketing Expert and C4:3 Urban Transport Planner) mobilized to support and train the UTMS in operation of BRT, parking and NMT. UTMS staff capacity building will be further strengthen through support PIC. Data Source: UTMS reports Actual value:

Output: 1. An urban transport management section (UTMS) for Vientiane established Indicator: Agency established and staff working, with 30% of staff being female by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Stakeholder confirmed that, staff to work in UTMS will be female focused and at least 30% are women, including management and decision making position members. Data Source: Implementation and Monitoring Consultants' reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 1. An urban transport management section (UTMS) for Vientiane established Indicator: Agency organizational arrangements approved by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
The “Sustainable Urban Transport Management Authority (SUTMA)” was changed to “Urban Transport Management Section (UTMS)". The establishment of UTMS has been approved on 7 April 2023. Key staff have been appointed (7 people. 1 woman). More staff will be appointed, with women are priority.
Capacity building of designated staff was started with the support of TRTA in September 2022, and to be continue through hands-on coating by the PIC consultants. Data Source: Implementation and Monitoring Consultants' reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: Bus maintenance facility operational by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Construction of BRT control, operations, maintenance, and fare system operating control center are ongoing and prepared a final acceptance check of the spare parts, tools and chargers for the readiness to hand over the 55 E-buses to the client - target to complete by Q2 2026. Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 2. High-quality bus services and bus rapid transit (BRT) operating in Vientiane Indicator: Control center and fare system operating by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Construction of BRT control, operations, maintenance, and fare system operating control center, connecting of the electricity to the depot and charging stations for the buses are ongoing - the overall progress at 96%.
The final testing of the ITS and traffic control systems, and training for drivers, and operations staff are depends on the BRT Operator ready - target to complete by Q2 2026.
Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 3. Traffic management in the core area of Vientiane improved Indicator: Road markings and signs installed by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
Road furniture, marking and signs installation works are included in the 3 contracts for BRT bus lens and stations, which being construction and complete in 2026 Data Source: Vientiane DPWT reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 4. Paid parking system and national vehicle registration system established Indicator: On-street paid parking scheme, using mobile phone application, operational in core area of Vientiane by 2026 Achievement: N Progress/Status: Ongoing.
A new on-street paid parking system for Vientiane's core area will be established that uses electronic meter technology. The new parking system will provide 2,100 on-street parking spaces for cars and 1,800 spaces for motorcycles. Also, a national electronic vehicle registration system will be established that facilitates enforcement of parking regulations. Both the parking and electronic vehicle registration systems will be implemented by private firms.
The parking regulations have not been endorsed, requiring immediate attention from relevant officials. Until such approval is secured, parking management activities in the 8 selected areas can be proceeded with Parking Management System by Q3 2025. Data Source: UTMS reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: N
